newsitem.title: USA: NY Times names Bill Keller managing editor.
newsitem.headline: NY Times names Bill Keller managing editor.

text.p: The New York Times said Thursday that it has named Bill Keller managing editor, replacing Gene Roberts, who has completed a three-year tour as managing editor while on leave as a professor at the University of Maryland.
Keller, said the company, becomes the second-highest editor at the newspaper. He will work as Roberts's deputy for an orientation period starting July 1 until Roberts leaves his position in the fall.
Keller joined the Times in 1984 as a Washington correspondant and won a Pulitzer Prize in 1989 for his coverage of the Soviet Union.
The company also named Gerald Boyd deputy managing editor for news, effective July 1. Boyd is currently an assistant managing editor, and joined the Times in 1983 as a White House correspondant.
John Geddes, currently business and financial editor, was named deputy managing editor for operations, effective September 1. He joined the newspaper as a business editor in 1994.
